title: REST, JSON and the contract the API promises to honour

videos.script: A test needs something to be right against. For an API, that something is a contract. {{contract}} This lesson reads boxoffice the way its clients do. First as resources, each with an address. {{resources}} Then as JSON, the text every answer is written in. JSON looks simple, and it hides three traps. Money, dates and big numbers. {{json}} Then you write the contract down. It is a file called openapi.yaml, and it says what boxoffice promises. Every path, every field, every status code. {{openapi}} Errors are part of that promise. boxoffice reports every one of them in the same shape, and a client depends on it. {{errors}} Last, you turn the contract into test cases. Zero seats, six, seven. A number sent as text. A field nobody asked for. {{cases}} Some of them break boxoffice. One request makes it crash. {{crash}} By the end, you know what the API owes its clients, and how to check that it pays.
